title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: There exist $C, C' > 0$ such that, for any simple graph $G$ that is embeddable on a surface of Euler genus $g$, if every edge is assigned at most $Ck$ conflicts from $[k]^2$, then $G$ is conflict $k$-colourable, provided $k \geq C'\sqrt{g}$.
context_text: In the conflict $k$-colouring problem (introduced by Dvořák and Postle, and by Fraigniaud, Heinrich and Kosowski), each edge $uv$ of a graph $G$ is assigned a list of ordered pairs, called conflicts, of colours from $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$, and one asks for a colouring $c:V\to[k]$ such that no edge is in a conflict, i.e. there is no edge $uv$ and conflict $(\kappa_u,\kappa_v)$ on it with $c(u)=\kappa_u$ and $c(v)=\kappa_v$. Having at most $\mu$ conflicts per edge is equivalent to having exactly one conflict per edge in a multigraph of maximum edge multiplicity $\mu$: a local $k$-partition of a multigraph is a family of maps $\kappa_v:E(v)\to[k]$ ($E(v)$ the edges at $v$), the edge $e=uv$ forbidding $c(u)=\kappa_u(e)$ together with $c(v)=\kappa_v(e)$; the single-conflict chromatic number $\chi_=(G)$ is the least $k$ such that $G$ is conflict-colourable for every local $k$-partition. It is at least the adaptable choosability and the separation choosability of $G$. The authors prove that for a multigraph of maximum multiplicity $\mu$ embeddable on a surface of Euler genus $g$, $\chi_=(G)\le\max\{C_1\sqrt{\mu}(g+1)^{1/4}\log(\mu^2(g+2)),8\mu\}$; in the regime $\mu=\Theta(\sqrt g)$ this gives $\chi_=(G)=O(\sqrt g\log g)$, evocative of Heawood's bound since both the number of colours and the multiplicity are around $\sqrt g$, and the conjecture asks to remove the logarithmic factor. The authors note that necessarily $C<1/2$, because of an example built from $K_{2,(2\mu)^2}$ with every edge of multiplicity $\mu$ (a planar multigraph with $\chi_=>2\mu$), and that a previous version of the manuscript incorrectly conjectured that $C$ could be taken arbitrarily close to $1$.

title: Škrekovski Conjecture (separation choosability of planar graphs)
statement_text: Every planar graph has separation choosability at most $3$.
context_text: The paper notes that this conjecture by Škrekovski [18] remains open to the best of the authors' knowledge. If true, it would imply that separation choosability and adaptable choosability can be distinct for some planar graphs, since Hell and Zhu exhibited planar graphs with adaptable chromatic number at least 4.
paper_contribution: The paper does not prove new results about this conjecture; it is mentioned in the context of comparing separation choosability and adaptable choosability for planar graphs.
notes: Citation [18] in the paper; year not recoverable from the provided text.

title: Informal conjecture on single-conflict chromatic number of degenerate graphs
statement_text: There might yet be some constant $C' > 0$ such that the single-conflict chromatic number of any $d$-degenerate graph on $n$ vertices is at most $C'\sqrt{d}\log n$.
context_text: In the conflict $k$-colouring problem (introduced by Dvořák and Postle, and by Fraigniaud, Heinrich and Kosowski), each edge $uv$ of a graph $G$ is assigned a list of ordered pairs, called conflicts, of colours from $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$, and one asks for a colouring $c:V\to[k]$ such that no edge is in a conflict, i.e. there is no edge $uv$ and conflict $(\kappa_u,\kappa_v)$ on it with $c(u)=\kappa_u$ and $c(v)=\kappa_v$. Having at most $\mu$ conflicts per edge is equivalent to having exactly one conflict per edge in a multigraph of maximum edge multiplicity $\mu$: a local $k$-partition of a multigraph is a family of maps $\kappa_v:E(v)\to[k]$ ($E(v)$ the edges at $v$), the edge $e=uv$ forbidding $c(u)=\kappa_u(e)$ together with $c(v)=\kappa_v(e)$; the single-conflict chromatic number $\chi_=(G)$ is the least $k$ such that $G$ is conflict-colourable for every local $k$-partition. It is at least the adaptable choosability and the separation choosability of $G$. A graph is $d$-degenerate if each of its subgraphs has a vertex of degree at most $d$. The authors prove that a simple graph embeddable on a surface of Euler genus $g$ has $\chi_=(G)\le C(g+1)^{1/4}\log(g+2)$, and wonder whether degeneracy could give an alternative proof, as in Heawood's original approach for the chromatic number. A construction of Kostochka and Zhu shows that $d$-degenerate graphs can have single-conflict chromatic number greater than $d$, but the bound $C'\sqrt d\log n$ would still imply the surface result in the simple-graph case. The authors' general bound $\chi_=(G)\le C_2(\mu m)^{1/4}\log(\mu m)$ for multigraphs with $m\ge3$ edges and maximum multiplicity $\mu$ gives only $C_2(nd)^{1/4}\log(nd)$ here; they say they have not been able to prove the $\sqrt d\log n$ bound.
notes: Stated as 'there might yet be' and 'we have not been able to prove this thus far'; clearly conjectural but not a labelled environment.
